summary:
LANE I, ONE ROW (ep 6), NO ANCHORS — dragon-ball-super is a PARALLEL telling (I40, Sean 2026-08-28): standing is from-the-outline-or-not, chapter numbers are CORRESPONDENCE, never anchors. THE ASK, ANSWERED FROM THE PAGES OF ch 1-4 (Toyotarō's four-chapter Battle of Gods digest, 65 pp; Kanzenshuu's per-chapter synopses + page breakdowns and the fandom's chapter pages read against each other):

(1) WHAT EACH CHAPTER CARRIES OF THE BIRTHDAY-PARTY VISIT. ch 1 (16 pp, vol 1 pp 6-22) — ABSENT: Goku farming, Beerus's banquet planet, Mr Satan's prize, the Kais; no Earth party. ch 2 (15 pp, pp 23-37) — NOT STAGED, SET UP: Whis places the surviving Saiyans on Earth, Beerus knocks Goku out and 'Beerus and Whis depart to Earth to question the other Saiyans', and the chapter's last panel has the two approaching Earth (Kanzenshuu ch 2: 'As the two approach Earth…'; fandom ch 2: 'Beerus and Whis then arrive above Earth.'). That closing page IS ep 6's premise. ch 3 (15 pp, pp 39-53) — NARRATED, plus ONE BEAT STAGED. Kanzenshuu's ch-3 synopsis, second paragraph, is the manga's whole account of the visit: 'Back on Earth, Bulma's cruise-ship-birthday-party has been interrupted by Beerus, who has stopped by to inquire about this supposed “Super Saiyan God”. Boo had apparently eaten all the pudding, leading Beerus to take out his frustration on the attendees.' The fandom's independent summary of the same pages carries the two lines that do the narrating in-panel — Beerus 'only went to Earth to ask about the Super Saiyan God but was given a rude introduction', and 'Beerus explaining that he wanted to try pudding, Gotenks replied back by saying that Majin Buu ate it' — and ch 3's first page has Goku, on King Kai's planet, naming the destination ('Beerus is heading to Earth and Bulma is having her birthday party'). SO THE REVIEWER'S CLAIM IS RIGHT AND THE STORED NOTE IS TOO STRONG: ch 3 narrates the pudding quarrel (it does not stage it). And one thing ep 6 stages is staged in ch 3 too: Vegeta's childhood flashback of Beerus standing atop King Vegeta ('This chapter marks the debut of King Vegeta in the manga'; Kanzenshuu: 'Vegeta has a flashback to a childhood memory of Beerus standing atop King Vegeta') — in the anime that flashback exists ONLY in ep 6 (fandom ep 6 + Kanzenshuu ep 6, both put it at Beerus's paralysing gaze). ch 4 (19 pp, pp 55-73) — ABSENT as staging, DEPENDENT as plot: Shenlong, the six-Saiyan ritual, Videl's pregnancy and the fight all play on and above the party ship. TWO MORE MANGA PAGES ON THE NODE: vol 1's between-chapter bonus drawings sit at p 38 and p 54, i.e. immediately before and after ch 3 (Kanzenshuu's vol-1 chapter table gives the starts 23 / 39 / 55, so exactly one filler page after ch 2 and one after ch 3) — the first shows Vegeta watching and mimicking dancers on TV (the bingo preparation), the second Vegeta disappointed that he never got to show the moves off. Toyotarō's own pages therefore treat the party visit as having HAPPENED in the manga's telling, with Vegeta's placating attempt elided.

(2) WHAT LATER BEATS DEPEND ON IT — IN BOTH TELLINGS. MANGA: ch 3's Earth half is a fight already in progress AT the party, whose stated cause is the pudding Buu ate at it; Bulma walks up and slaps Beerus 'for ruining her party' (fandom: 'for causing a commotion during her party'), Beerus slaps her back, and that is the trigger for Vegeta's rage — the manga's own next chapter; ch 4 then summons Shenlong on that ship, needs six pure-hearted Saiyans and gets them because Bulma's party is where the family is, and reveals Videl's pregnancy there. ANIME: eps 7-14 run the identical chain. Remove the visit and neither telling's next chapter/episode has a setting, a cause or a cast. CONTRAST ep 4 (Pilaf, ruled D 2026-08-28): nothing later in either telling depends on the Pilaf boarding. So ep 6 is NOT D.

(3) THE STANDING: CANON. Under T30 this clears the load-bearing test twice over — as B (an anime-staged node of a shared arc whose later beats both tellings depend on, with the manga's version citable: ch 3's narration) and, for one beat, as C (the King Vegeta flashback is staged in both). There is no story-carrying D block in the episode: every beat is the film's (ja-WP's 神と神 あらすじ has the party, Vegeta's dance, the pudding quarrel and the childhood memory), and the one Toei substitution — the octopus/wasabi-takoyaki business standing in for the film's bingo song (Kanzenshuu ep 6, Episode Notes) — is a different staging of the same node, a divergence, not an original plot. So canon, not mixed. MECHANICAL WARNING (see flags): the row's only source-side record is side_source{the film} with no adopted{basis}, and lib/side-source.ts defaults exactly that shape to FILLER at every write; its weight-bearing escape list is anchor / chain_source / side_story / unverified — and an anchor is FORBIDDEN on a parallel series. A canon standing on ep 6 can only survive as a T6 pin (EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES), the way 50 / 78 / 90 / 91 already do.

RECAP BASELINE — ep 6 — stored: filler [+ side_source] → proposed: canon (annotation added: divergence{3}; side_source KEPT, its note repaired; no adopted, no anchor).

type_corrections.why: T30's load-bearing test on a SHARED arc (A46: Battle of Gods, eps 1-14 ↔ ch 1-4, both tellings descending from the 2013 film). FILLER on this series means D — studio padding no telling's story depends on — and ep 6 fails that test on the manga's own pages. (a) The manga NARRATES the visit rather than ignoring it: ch 3's opening Earth pages say Bulma's cruise-ship birthday party 'has been interrupted by Beerus, who has stopped by to inquire about this supposed “Super Saiyan God”' and that 'Boo had apparently eaten all the pudding, leading Beerus to take out his frustration on the attendees' (Kanzenshuu chp-03); the fandom's reading of the same pages has the in-panel lines — Beerus 'was given a rude introduction', Gotenks 'Majin Buu ate it' — and ch 3's first page has Goku name the party as Beerus's destination. (b) One beat of ep 6 is STAGED in the manga: Vegeta's childhood flashback of Beerus atop King Vegeta (ch 3; 'the debut of King Vegeta in the manga'), which in the anime is in ep 6 and nowhere else. (c) The manga's later beats depend on the visit: ch 3's fight happens at the party, is caused by the pudding, and turns on Bulma slapping Beerus for ruining her party; ch 4's ritual, Videl's pregnancy reveal and the Goku/Beerus rematch all play on and above that ship. (d) Nothing in the episode is an original story block: every beat is in the film both tellings descend from (ja-WP 神と神 あらすじ: the party, Vegeta's dance, the pudding quarrel, the childhood memory of Beerus on Planet Vegeta, the Pilaf gang aboard), and the sole Toei substitution — the octopus and the wasabi-takoyaki gag replacing the film's bingo song (Kanzenshuu ep 6 Episode Notes) — is a different staging of the same node. Same node, different telling = divergence on a canon row, the instrument this series already uses on eps 1-2 / 79-81 / 94-95. So: canon as B (an anime-staged, load-bearing node of a shared arc, with the manga's version citable) and, for the flashback, as C. NOT mixed: there is no story-carrying original share (T28). This is NOT an adoption argument — no adopted{author} is proposed and none is needed; the 脚本 bar (Resurrection 'F') is settled and this film's 脚本 is 渡辺雄介. The stored filler is the T26 writer default of 2026-09-05 (a placeholder, per the ask), and it can only be replaced by a T6 pin — see the flags.

annotations.note: Same node, different telling (the series' established kind on canon rows — eps 1-2, 79-81, 94-95; NOT 'rearranged', which A45 retired on this parallel series). The anime STAGES the birthday-party visit across ep 6: Beerus and Whis board the Princess Bulma, Vegeta is paralysed and remembers Beerus atop King Vegeta, Beerus questions him about the Super Saiyan God, Bulma takes the pair round the party, the takoyaki/octopus placating, then Buu refuses the pudding and is knocked aside. The manga's ch 3 COMPRESSES the same node into narration on its opening Earth pages — the party 'has been interrupted by Beerus, who has stopped by to inquire about this supposed Super Saiyan God'; 'Boo had apparently eaten all the pudding, leading Beerus to take out his frustration on the attendees'; in-panel, Beerus 'was given a rude introduction' and Gotenks answers that Buu ate the pudding — and stages only the King Vegeta flashback, relocated from Beerus's arrival (anime/film) to the middle of the fight (manga). weight: SIGNIFICANT for the row's standing under I40/T30 — not because ch 3's narration is large (it is two sentences) but because the node it narrates is the one ch 3's fight and ch 4's ritual both stand on; ep 6 is the only telling that stages it. Three tellings, kept apart: the FILM stages the visit with Vegeta's bingo song (ja-WP あらすじ); the ANIME substitutes the octopus/wasabi-takoyaki business (Kanzenshuu ep 6 Episode Notes); the MANGA elides the placating altogether and jokes about it on vol 1's bonus pages either side of ch 3 (p 38 Vegeta mimicking TV dancers, p 54 Vegeta disappointed he never got to show the moves off).

correspondence.note: THE CORRESPONDENCE ROW THE ASK REQUESTS. Divergent, not anime_only: the digest does carry the node, in two forms. (i) NARRATED — ch 3's opening Earth pages state the visit and its outcome in retrospect (Kanzenshuu chp-03: the party 'has been interrupted by Beerus, who has stopped by to inquire about this supposed Super Saiyan God'; 'Boo had apparently eaten all the pudding, leading Beerus to take out his frustration on the attendees'); ch 3's first page also names the party from King Kai's planet. (ii) STAGED — ch 3 draws Vegeta's childhood flashback of Beerus standing atop King Vegeta, the one ep-6 beat the manga also stages (anime-side it is in ep 6 only). SETUP: the node's manga setup is ch 2's closing page (Beerus and Whis leave Goku 'to question the other Saiyans' and approach Earth). NOT CARRIED BY THE DIGEST (the anime's/film's staging): Bulma welcoming the pair aboard, Yamcha's over-familiarity, Krillin's wasabi takoyaki, the squirt-gun soaking, Vegeta's octopus, the Pilaf thread, the pudding refusal and Buu vs Beerus as scenes. DISSENT RECORDED: Kanzenshuu's ch-3 Chapter Note says the chapter 'skips all of the setup in episode six of the TV series to jump straight to the essential material from episodes seven and eight', and the fandom's ch-3 episode= field names only eps 7 and 8 — both true of the SETUP and both silent on the flashback that its own synopsis describes. The fandom's ep-6 page prints the boilerplate 'The entire events of this episode were exclusive to the anime', which the chapter page's own summary refutes (and whose trivia section then compares the ep-6 flashback with the FILM's version of it).

The staging half of the same row, kept separate so the map does not over-claim: the visit as SCENES — Bulma welcoming Beerus and Whis aboard the Princess Bulma, Beerus questioning Vegeta about the Super Saiyan God, Yamcha and the wasabi takoyaki, Goten/Trunks's squirt guns, Vegeta diving for the octopus and cooking it, Buu hogging the pudding, Mr Satan knocked aside, Buu vs Beerus — appears in no chapter of the digest. It is the FILM's sequence (ja-WP 神と神 あらすじ), with Toei substituting the octopus/takoyaki for the film's bingo song (Kanzenshuu ep 6). Recorded as correspondence, not as a standing: under I40/T30 an anime-only staging of a load-bearing shared node is B, i.e. canon.

repairs.old: Battle of Gods (the 2013 film 『ドラゴンボールZ 神と神』): the birthday-party sequence is the film's, not the manga's — the manga's four-chapter digest has nothing here (ch 3's episode index omits ep 6 and its summary carries none of it). The batch-19 film precedent (Resurrection 'F' rows 18-27).
repairs.new: Battle of Gods (the 2013 film 『ドラゴンボールZ 神と神』; 脚本 渡辺雄介, 原作・ストーリー 鳥山明): ep 6 stages the film's birthday-party visit (Beerus and Whis boarding the Princess Bulma, Vegeta's placating, the pudding quarrel, Buu vs Beerus). The manga's four-chapter digest does not STAGE the visit — but it is not silent on it: ch 3's opening Earth pages NARRATE it (Beerus 'has stopped by to inquire about this supposed Super Saiyan God'; 'Boo had apparently eaten all the pudding, leading Beerus to take out his frustration on the attendees' — Kanzenshuu; Beerus's own line 'was given a rude introduction' and Gotenks's 'Majin Buu ate it' — fandom), ch 3 STAGES one beat the anime stages only in ep 6 (Vegeta's childhood flashback of Beerus atop King Vegeta — 'the debut of King Vegeta in the manga'), and vol 1's between-chapter bonus pages bracket the visit from the manga's side (p 38: Vegeta mimicking dancers on TV; p 54: Vegeta disappointed he never got to show the bingo moves off). Under I40/T30 the node is load-bearing in BOTH tellings — ch 3's fight, Bulma's slap 'for ruining her party' and ch 4's whole ritual play at that party — so the row is canon (B/C), not D. The side_source record stays; NO adopted{author} (the author bar is 脚本, and this film's 脚本 is 渡辺雄介).
repairs.why: Note-only repair on the stored I40 side_source record (ruling-tier, Sean 2026-08-28, lifted from the wave-5a verdict): the annotation KIND and its work label are unchanged and no adoption is proposed. Two of the stored note's clauses do not survive the pages. (1) 'the manga's four-chapter digest has nothing here' — ch 3's opening Earth pages narrate the visit and its pudding cause, and ch 3 stages the King Vegeta flashback that the anime stages only in ep 6; vol 1's bonus pages at p 38 and p 54 bracket the elided placating. (2) 'ch 3's episode index omits ep 6' — that is SILENCE (a wiki field), not evidence, and the wave-5a verdict's stronger form ('ep 6 really has ZERO manga pages') is refuted by the same wiki's own chapter summary and by Kanzenshuu's. What the stored note got right is kept: the birthday-party sequence as STAGED is the film's, and the manga stages no part of it apart from the flashback.

structure.notes:
=== 1. ROW IDENTITY (R20, checked before anything else) === Our row 6 = 'Don't Anger the God of Destruction! Excitement at the Birthday Party', aired 2015-08-16. dragonball.fandom's page (localised title 'Don't Anger the Destroyer! A Heart-Pounding Birthday Party') gives Airdate = August 16, 2015 and Number = 6; Kanzenshuu's eps-006 gives '16 August 2015 (9:00-9:30AM, Sunday, Fuji TV)'; ja-WP's episode table row 6 gives 8月16日 / 破壊神を怒らせるな! ドキドキ誕生日パーティー. Same row on three sources, joined on title+date, never index.

=== 2. THE CORRESPONDENCE-ROW PROPOSAL (the ask's deliverable (3)) ===
{ episode: 6, chapters: '3', alignment: 'divergent', note: 'ch 3's opening Earth pages NARRATE the party visit (the interruption, Beerus's Super-Saiyan-God errand, Buu having eaten the pudding) and STAGE one of ep 6's beats (Vegeta's childhood flashback of Beerus atop King Vegeta, relocated into the fight); ch 2's closing page is the setup (Beerus and Whis leave for Earth to question the other Saiyans). The visit AS SCENES is the film's and the anime's only.', sources: [Kanzenshuu chp-03, dragonball.fandom ch 3, Kanzenshuu chp-02, dragonball.fandom ch 2, Kanzenshuu eps-006, dragonball.fandom ep 6] }
A second row is delivered for the staging half: { episode: 6, chapters: null, alignment: 'anime_only', note: the party visit as scenes appears in no chapter of the digest — it is the film's sequence with the octopus/takoyaki substituted for the bingo song }. Two rows, because one range cannot say both things and the instrument allows several rows per episode (the wave-5d precedent on ep 4: one anime_only row + one divergent row for a closing fragment).
NOT ANIME_ONLY as the single verdict: the boilerplate answer ('the digest carries nothing of the node') is what the pages refute.

=== 3. THE BATTLE OF GODS DIGEST, CHAPTER BY CHAPTER, AGAINST THE PARTY VISIT ===
| chapter | pp (vol 1) | the party visit | evidence |
| ch 1 破壊神の予知夢 | 16 pp, 6-22 | ABSENT | Goku farming / Beerus's banquet planet / Mr Satan's prize / the Kais (fandom ch 1; Kanzenshuu arc synopsis) |
| ch 2 悟空の敗北 | 15 pp, 23-37 | NOT STAGED, SET UP — the chapter ends with Beerus and Whis leaving 'to question the other Saiyans' and approaching Earth | Kanzenshuu chp-02 final paragraph; fandom ch 2 ('Beerus and Whis then arrive above Earth.') |
| bonus p 38 | 1 p | REFERENCED — Vegeta watching and mimicking dancers on TV (the bingo preparation) | fandom ch 2 trivia + gallery ('Vegeta Bingo Dance (manga).jpg'); Kanzenshuu vol-01 ('new drawings between chapters… such as Vegeta practicing bingo'); the chapter starts 23/39/55 leave exactly one page after ch 2 and one after ch 3 |
| ch 3 ビルスの怒り | 15 pp, 39-53 | NARRATED (the interruption, the errand, the pudding) + ONE BEAT STAGED (the King Vegeta flashback) | Kanzenshuu chp-03 ¶2; fandom ch 3 summary, Appearances (King Vegeta {D}) and trivia ('marks the debut of King Vegeta in the manga') |
| bonus p 54 | 1 p | REFERENCED — Vegeta disappointed he never got to show the bingo moves off | fandom ch 3 trivia + gallery ('Bingo2.jpg'); Kanzenshuu vol-01 |
| ch 4 神と神 | 19 pp, 55-73 | ABSENT as staging, DEPENDENT as plot (Shenlong, the six-Saiyan ritual, Videl's pregnancy, the rematch — all on and above the party ship) | Kanzenshuu chp-04; fandom ch 4 |
Digest total 65 pp (Kanzenshuu arc page), of which the two chapters that stand on the party visit (ch 3 + ch 4) are 34 pp.

=== 4. WHAT DEPENDS ON THE NODE (the ask's deliverable (2)) ===
MANGA: ch 3 — the fight is already in progress AT the party when the chapter cuts to Earth; the pudding is its stated cause; Bulma slaps Beerus 'for causing a commotion during her party' and his return slap triggers Vegeta's rage (the chapter's climax, and the anime's ep 7). ch 4 — Shenlong is summoned on the ship; the ritual needs six pure-hearted Saiyans and finds them because the family is at Bulma's party; Videl's pregnancy is revealed there; the Goku/Beerus fight starts above the liner. ANIME: eps 7-14 in the identical order. FILM: the same, and the film RESTARTS the party at the end ('その後、ブルマの誕生パーティーが再開される中' — ja-WP). So the visit is the arc's hinge in every telling. The negative control is ep 4 (Pilaf, ruled D 2026-08-28): its boarding subplot is referenced by nothing later in either telling, and the manga's only tie there is a closing graft of ch 2's opening beats.

=== 5. THE THREE TELLINGS, KEPT APART (the ask's trap) ===
FILM (神と神, 2013, 脚本 渡辺雄介 / 原案 鳥山明): stages the visit; Vegeta placates with a bingo song and dance; the pudding quarrel; the childhood memory of Beerus on Planet Vegeta; the Pilaf gang aboard (ja-WP あらすじ + character notes). ANIME ep 6: stages the same sequence, substituting the octopus and the wasabi-takoyaki gag for the bingo song (Kanzenshuu eps-006 Episode Notes, explicitly comparing the two), and drawing young Vegeta with bangs where the film drew him with adult hair (fandom ep 6 trivia — itself proof the beat is the film's, not anime-original). MANGA ch 3: narrates the visit, stages the flashback in a different position, and jokes on the bonus pages about the placating it cut. None of these three facts is quoted as another's.

=== 6. WHY NO ANCHOR (A46 / I40) === This series never anchors: the anime and the manga are two realizations of one unpublished Toriyama text (ja-WP 漫画版: the outline is delivered as text and both staffs work 同時進行 from it), so chapter numbers are correspondence, not position. anchors: [], continue_points: [], anchor_hostile: [] — and no row in this verdict could take an anchor later.

=== 7. SOURCE TIERS === Primary and read directly: dragonball.fandom via the MediaWiki API (chapter pages 1-4, episode pages 6 and 7), Kanzenshuu's Manga Guide (the Battle of Gods arc page, chp-02/03/04, tankobon vol-01) and Episode Guide (eps-006), ja-WP ドラゴンボールZ 神と神 and ドラゴンボール超. Kanzenshuu and the fandom are independent of each other (different editors, different framing; they disagree in the ways recorded above). No instant-answer box, no content farm, no MangaBaka; MangaPlus's API refused (403) so no page images were read — the page-level claims here rest on two independent per-chapter synopses plus the volume's own page numbering, which is stated as such rather than as a panel count.

flags_for_sean: MECHANICAL — A CANON ep 6 NEEDS A T6 PIN, OR THE WRITER WILL PUT IT BACK TO FILLER. lib/side-source.ts defaults a canon/mixed row whose only source-side record is an unadopted side_source to FILLER, unless the row has a weight-bearing tie: an anchor, chain_source, side_story or unverified. Ep 6 can never have an anchor — anchors are FORBIDDEN on a parallel series (I40/A46) and the apply script throws on one. So the standing this verdict proposes can only land as an EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES (T6) pin, alongside the existing 50 / 78 / 90 / 91. Please rule the pin explicitly if you accept the retype.

RULE QUESTION (not acted on) — T26's WEIGHT-BEARING LIST HAS NO ENTRY FOR A PARALLEL SERIES. On an I40 series the catalog's tie to the source is the episode_correspondence row, not an anchor; T26's escape list (anchor / chain_source / side_story / unverified) therefore cannot be satisfied by any row of dragon-ball-super, and every side_source row on a parallel series is structurally filler regardless of evidence. Ep 6 is the first row where that bites. Options: (a) leave it to T6 pins (what this verdict assumes), or (b) let a divergent/aligned correspondence row count as a weight-bearing tie on isParallelSeries series. A gate question, not a research one.

A STANDING HAZARD IN THE ARC — DO NOT STAMP side_source ACROSS eps 1-14. The wave-5a verdict offered, as an alternative, extending side_source{Battle of Gods film} to the whole arc 'for consistency'. Since the T26 sitting (2026-09-05) that would now flip every one of those rows to filler at the next write, including rows with real ch 1-4 correspondence (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9-14). If the arc's film parentage is to be recorded consistently, it belongs in the A46 ARC note, not as per-row side_source.

SOURCE BOILERPLATE THAT FAILED, BOTH WAYS — dragonball.fandom's ep-6 page prints 'Differences from the manga: The entire events of this episode were exclusive to the anime', which the SAME wiki's ch-3 page refutes (the King Vegeta flashback, the narrated pudding); and the same page's trivia then compares the ep-6 flashback with the FILM's version of it. Kanzenshuu's ch-3 Chapter Note ('skips all of the setup in episode six… to jump straight to the essential material from episodes seven and eight') is right about the setup and silent about the flashback its own synopsis describes. Both are recorded in the verdict rather than resolved by preference — the pages carried the decision.

THE ASK'S TWO PREMISES, TESTED, NEITHER QUOTED AS EVIDENCE — the stored note's 'the digest has nothing here' is REFUTED (narration + one staged beat + two bonus pages); the reviewer's 'ch 3 narrates the pudding quarrel' is CONFIRMED (narrated, not staged — Kanzenshuu chp-03 and the fandom's ch-3 summary independently). No adopted{author} is proposed anywhere in this verdict; the side_source record stays as ruled.
